title: Global stocks rally as investors shrug off new U.S. tariffs
dek: Markets rise as traders look for bargains after the White House announces tariffs on more than a dozen trading partners
body:
Global equity markets rally after the White House unveils a fresh set of tariffs and investors appear to push aside recent AI-related worries. CNBC reports traders are "fishing for bargains," buying stocks despite the new trade measures.

## Why it matters

The move matters because tariffs change the cost calculus for exporters, importers and multinational supply chains — and markets are signaling a willingness to look through near-term policy risk. The reaction also shows investors are prioritizing valuations and potential buying opportunities over headline risk from both trade policy and AI developments. That affects capital flows, corporate planning and short-term volatility across equities.

## The details

- The White House announced a set of tariffs on Wednesday. CNBC reports the tariffs target more than a dozen major trading partners.
- Global stocks rallied after the announcement, with investors described by CNBC as "fishing for bargains." 
- CNBC links the rally to investors shrugging off both the tariff announcement and recent AI jitters. 
- Specifics about which countries or sectors face the tariffs are not reported in CNBC's summary. 
- CNBC's reporting does not provide details on tariff rates, implementation timelines, exemptions, or immediate market-moving statements from affected governments.

## What to watch

Watch official documentation from the White House for the list of affected countries, tariff rates and effective dates; those details will determine which industries face the largest cost increases. Also watch corporate guidance from exporters and multinational firms for near-term impacts on supply chains and earnings assumptions.

Source: reporting by CNBC.
author: Kelvane Club Desk
